answer: Each household turns its compost pit weekly, and the pit keeper measures the pits and records the turning in the book. A garden pit claimed as turned fails the record: at the sonnet of the pit the compost must show the turning the keeper himself measured, and an unturned pit smells of rot. Faking a compost season takes a keeper, twelve weeks of false entries and 5,400 in wages, and the onyx entry in the pit book is checked at every planting, so a pit whose turning was never recorded is emptied by the village.
